chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: Deluxe Melody Boys and George Corley's Royal Aces
summary: Cousins sang with the Deluxe Melody Boys, which became George Corley's Royal Aces, where Ramey started late 1931.

bands.name: George Corley and His Royal Aces

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And at the same time they, my brothers and my cousins, they'd sing in quartets. And then this Ira Glasgow, he went on to sing in that Deluxe Melody Boys Band.
Well, now, where did they operate?
They were in Austin, and around, but they did some touring, you know.
Did any famous people come out of

Well, I don't know whether Buddy Tate came there to work with them or not. Herschel -- and I worked with Herschel in Texas, and I didn't do much, because I couldn't play, you know. But I was going through the motions.
Herschel , he was with another band.
What you're talking of here with I mean the Deluxe Melody Boys, this is when? Around '28, or something? How old would you be?
Well, the Deluxe Melody Boys would and went be -- I guess they started about '26 up to until about 1930, or '31.
And this would be around Austin, mostly, would it?
Yeah, they was all local musicians. And then George Corley (PHONETIC) took it over, and that it became George Corley and his Royal Aces.

Right. And he took it over. Now, there was three brothers in that one, Reginald played trumpet, he's teaching school down in Washington, and I think he's retired now, but he gave up the music business and was teaching in Washington. George was playing in San Francisco,
he played trombone. And Wilfred, he was about my age, he's retired and is living in Austin.

Now, that's -- when I first started working in that band, it was in 1932, very shortly, because -- actually I started in '39 -- I mean, the last part of '31. And worked up until the time I went away to college.
